guides.title: Chaco Canyon
guides.description: Great houses, small houses, regional outliers and roads.

guides.title: Hovenweep
guides.description: Separate settlement groups, towers, springs and agricultural landscape.

guides.title: Mesa Verde
guides.description: Cliff dwellings, mesa-top villages and changing settlement patterns.

guides.title: Canyons of the Ancients
guides.description: Lowry, Sand Canyon and the settlements around them.

guides.title: Machu Picchu and the Inca heartland
guides.description: Architecture, engineering, dated occupation and wider settlement / road connections.

guides.title: Maya centers and networks
guides.description: Individual centers, their civic buildings, reservoirs and inter-site connections.

guides.title: Cahokia and the American Bottom
guides.description: Mounds, plazas, neighborhoods, satellite communities and changing urban scale.

guides.title: Pacific complexes and island networks
guides.description: Nan Madol, monumental centers and island connections examined separately.

guides.title: Chaco culture and regional connections
guides.description: Ritual, language questions, growth and transformation, with a road-network map.

guides.title: Inca civilization and Qhapaq Ñan
guides.description: Religion, languages, imperial growth and transformation, and the road system.

guides.title: Maya cultures and histories
guides.description: Ritual, languages and changing political centers, distinguished from individual cities.

guides.title: Mississippian cultures and networks
guides.description: Diverse communities and traditions, ritual evidence, language limits, growth and transformation.

guides.title: Caral and the Supe Valley
guides.description: Caral was one place in an inhabited valley linked to the Pacific coast. This guide follows individual settlements and dated building observations, keeping construction samples separate from the long lives of communities.

guides.title: Kuk
guides.region: Papua New Guinea · upper Wahgi Valley
guides.description: Kuk preserves separate episodes of cultivation and water management in the New Guinea highlands. It is an agricultural landscape with changing practices, not a single town founded once and occupied unchanged for ten thousand years.

guides.title: Upano
guides.description: The Upano Valley contains named settlements, roads and engineered fields. This guide separates excavated places, proposed archaeological phases and a nearby environmental archive. They are related kinds of evidence, but they do not carry the same dates or precision.

guides.title: Chavín de Huántar
guides.description: Follow successive building projects and specific deposited objects at Chavín, with the disagreements between architectural and ceramic sequences kept visible.

guides.title: Tiwanaku
guides.description: A changing urban community, major monuments and later activity: follow what separate kinds of evidence say about the city’s growth and transformation.

guides.title: Chan Chan and Chimor
guides.description: Follow the growth and reorganization of adobe compounds, working communities and changing political authority without treating every wall as contemporary.

guides.title: Wari: cities, households and the Moquegua enclave
guides.description: Compare planned places and local observations in the Moquegua enclave. Separate building phases, household histories, exchange and evidence that remains unplaced.

guides.title: Moche: Huacas de Moche and a long-lived urban landscape
guides.description: Follow particular north-coast communities and construction contexts, rather than assigning every place to one uniform Moche state or one shared ending.

guides.title: Teotihuacan
guides.description: Look inside the city’s building sequence, changing apartment compounds and later tunnel occupations. Different neighbourhoods did not share one simple ending.

guides.title: Monte Albán
guides.description: Explore a hilltop city’s household works, inscriptions, ballcourt and tomb reuse, with competing interpretations of government and conquest.

guides.title: Calakmul
guides.description: Follow a Maya centre through construction, murals, royal inscriptions and later use, separating political titles from the lives of the people around them.

guides.title: Copán
guides.description: Explore buried architectural phases, Oropéndola and the Hieroglyphic Stairway, then the evidence for activity after royal monumental production changed.

guides.title: Paquimé
guides.description: Follow earlier houses, the multistorey town, animal husbandry and a directly dated interment. Wider connections did not make this place a copy of another city.

guides.title: Poverty Point
guides.description: Explore individually dated earthworks and habitation, and the materials connecting Poverty Point with a wider world.

guides.title: Hopewell earthworks
guides.description: Visit distinct earthwork complexes and compare their chronologies, ceremonial spaces and material connections without making them one city.

guides.title: San Agustín
guides.description: Follow local settlements, burial architecture and sculpture through their separate histories in the upper Magdalena.

guides.title: Tierradentro
guides.description: Explore named tomb groups alongside settlement evidence, distinguishing uncertain tomb dates from better-resolved local occupation phases.

guides.title: Casarabe urban landscapes
guides.description: Look at individual centers and engineered landscapes, separating dated construction, regional models and later agricultural evidence.

guides.title: Nan Madol: building, water and chiefly life
guides.description: Follow separate construction projects in Nan Madol and the evidence for changing use; an early tomb date is not the beginning of every islet.

guides.title: Budj Bim: an engineered water landscape
guides.description: Explore engineering and settlement in the Budj Bim cultural landscape with distinct dates for landforms, construction and continued use.

guides.title: Gunditjmara histories: Country, work and persistence
guides.description: Connect engineered Country with Gunditjmara community histories, colonial intrusion, coercive institutions and continuing agency.

guides.title: Lapita communities and successors
guides.region: Pacific · Island Melanesia and western Polynesia
guides.description: Follow particular settlements and connections across islands, then ask what changed after the archaeological label Lapita ceased to describe pottery.

guides.title: Aztec: building and remaking an Animas community
guides.description: A local chronology of construction, alteration, communal use, and living Pueblo connections at Aztec Ruins.

guides.title: Salmon: a great house through changing generations
guides.description: A local chronology distinguishing Salmon Pueblo’s first construction, continued occupation, later rebuilding, and final-use evidence.

guides.title: Canyon de Chelly / Tséyi’: a living homeland
guides.description: Follow distinct Pueblo building phases, a named Diné artistic attribution, military violence, forced removal and the 1931 monument within Navajo land. Feature points and broad historical anchors retain different geographic precision.

guides.title: Four Corners: connected histories and continuing homelands
guides.region: Southwestern United States · Four Corners and neighboring homelands
guides.description: Follow changing settlement, regional connections, migration, colonial coercion and continuing Pueblo, Diné and Ute histories from early farming communities to 1934.

guides.title: Pueblo Bonito: one house, several histories
guides.description: A close study of changing construction, unequal status and continued use within the larger Chaco history.

guides.title: Lowry Pueblo
guides.description: Four local views follow the pueblo and great kiva through construction and later maintenance.

guides.title: Sand Canyon Pueblo
guides.description: Three views separate village construction, occupation and terminal violence.

guides.title: Castle Rock Pueblo
guides.description: Three local views keep occupation, setting and evidence of violence distinct.

guides.title: Communities around Cortez
guides.description: Follow Lowry, Escalante, Dominguez, Sand Canyon, Castle Rock and Saddlehorn without inventing an ancient Cortez center.

guides.title: Yap rai: stone, sea crossings and social value
guides.description: Follow the full undertaking: negotiated quarry access in Palau, skilled manufacture, provisioning and ocean transport, then the relationships through which a stone mattered on Yap. The evidence distinguishes a quarry, a voyage and a transfer of ownership.

guides.title: Palau: inhabited islands, earthworks and connected shores
guides.description: Palau’s history is larger than its role in Yapese stone money. Follow early occupation, working landscapes, villages, maritime relationships and a major eighteenth-century encounter.

guides.title: Micronesia: island chains and many histories
guides.region: Marianas · Palau · Yap · Caroline and Marshall Islands
guides.description: Micronesia is a geographic frame for diverse communities and histories. Use the map to compare particular sites and connections, rather than reading one migration arrow as the story of every island.

guides.title: Borneo and Brunei
guides.region: Northern Borneo · Sarawak · Brunei · Labuan · Sabah
guides.description: Forests, sacred places, river capitals, labour and changing colonial powers.

guides.title: Cebu and its maritime neighbours
guides.description: Older boatbuilding and port connections, local political choices, colonial town building and export commerce.

guides.title: Timor
guides.description: Early fishing, hilltop communities, sandalwood commerce, local rulers and the making of colonial borders.

guides.title: New Guinea and neighbouring islands
guides.region: New Guinea · Bismarck Archipelago · south Papuan coast
guides.description: Highland cultivation and crafts, Lapita settlements, maritime partners and uneven colonial reach.

guides.title: Great Lakes and Ontario: waterways, villages and treaty country
guides.region: Canada — Ontario and the Great Lakes
guides.description: Fish fences, longhouse villages, canoe commerce and colonial institutions reveal a Great Lakes world built through work, diplomacy, conflict and continuing Indigenous community life.

guides.title: Québec and the St. Lawrence: villages, alliances and living homelands
guides.region: Canada — Québec and the St. Lawrence
guides.description: Follow stone-working places, farming villages, river diplomacy and colonial land changes while keeping the histories of Indigenous communities visible beyond every change of regime.

guides.title: Atlantic Canada: coastal communities, fisheries and displacement
guides.region: Canada — New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, Newfoundland and Labrador
guides.description: Deep coastal evidence, sea-going work and living Indigenous communities connect with colonial fisheries, Acadian displacement, treaty diplomacy and imposed schooling through 1934.

guides.title: Pacific Canada: shorelines, villages and colonial encounters
guides.description: Footprints, clam gardens, houses, trade and Indigenous communities across the coast and Fraser interior.

guides.title: Prairie Canada: foodways, Métis settlements and treaty encounters
guides.description: Hunting, cultivation, river-lot communities, treaties and colonial institutions across the northern plains.

guides.title: Northwest Canada: tools, trade and changing authority
guides.description: Ancient hunting technology, northern exchange, Klondike displacement and treaty encounters.

guides.title: Arctic Canada: houses, hunting and encounters with the state
guides.description: Local archaeological sequences, Inuit dwellings, whaling labour, trade and colonial institutions through 1934.

guides.title: Aleutian Islands: maritime communities, colonial pressures and continuity
guides.region: North Pacific — Aleutian and Pribilof islands
guides.description: The Aleutian and Pribilof islands hold histories of skilled maritime life, enduring villages and profound colonial disruption. Tools, houses, gardens, churches and working harbours reveal how Unangan communities lived and changed across the centuries before 1934.

guides.title: Canada: many histories, one shared map
guides.region: Northern North America — eight regional histories
guides.description: Explore eight regional histories of homes, food, travel, diplomacy and colonial change, from the earliest evidence to 1934.

guides.title: Amaknak Bridge
guides.description: Stone houses, floor channels, repairs and archaeological evidence of daily work.

guides.title: Iliuliuk and Unalaska
guides.description: A survey chart of the nineteenth-century village, successive churches and the earlier Reese Bay longhouse.

guides.title: Chaluka and Nikolski
guides.description: A layered settlement, stone-walled house, earlier island sites and the building phases of St. Nicholas Church.

guides.title: Canadian Shield — camps, waterways and inland communities
guides.region: Canada — Ontario, Québec, Manitoba, Saskatchewan, Labrador and Great Slave Lake
guides.description: Follow ancient hearths, sturgeon fisheries and portage routes from inland Labrador to Great Slave Lake, then see how fur trading, treaty-making and hydroelectric development changed life through 1934.

guides.title: Indigenous communities of Costa Rica and Panama
guides.description: Rivers, coastal networks, settlements and ceremonial places before and around Spanish contact

guides.title: Atlantic Brazil: mounds, villages and exchange
guides.region: Eastern, Atlantic and southern coastal Brazil
guides.description: Follow coastal mound builders, river villages, pottery-making communities and the materials that connected them.

guides.title: After Lapita in the Solomon Islands and Vanuatu
guides.description: Shoreline villages, gardens, shrines and voyages from the first millennium BCE to 1800 CE

guides.title: Northern Idaho’s rivers and gathering places
guides.description: Fishing and gathering on the Clearwater and neighboring rivers connect early archaeological evidence to Nimiipuu councils and two histories of mission building.

guides.title: Rapa Nui from Anakena to Haŋa Roa
guides.description: Follow coastal platforms, quarry gardens and ceremonial sites into the period of colonial agreements and restrictions on Rapanui people.

guides.title: Crossing the mountains in western Montana
guides.description: Painted shelters, trading posts and treaty grounds put several kinds of evidence on the routes across the northern Rocky Mountains.

guides.title: Windward Islands and Barbados
guides.description: Ceramic-age settlements and changes in fishing connect Grenada, Carriacou and Saint Lucia. Records from Barbados and Saint Lucia trace resistance and emancipation in the plantation era.

guides.title: Caddo communities and inland Louisiana
guides.description: Red River evidence follows Caddo mound and village landscapes into the trading frontier between the French and Spanish outposts.

guides.title: Marshes and homelands of northwestern Nevada
guides.description: The western Great Basin’s wetlands supported skilled work. Later sources follow Northern Paiute resistance and educational initiatives alongside military and federal institutions.

guides.title: Leeward islands of the northern Lesser Antilles
guides.description: Early ceramic-age sites and coastal settlements predate the forts and naval works built with enslaved labor.

guides.title: Communities of Venezuela’s rivers, llanos and islands
guides.description: Compare work on the Orinoco, drained fields in the Barinas llanos, and maritime activity on the cays off Venezuela’s coast.

guides.title: Fiji, Tonga and Samoa after initial settlement
guides.description: Dune deposits in Fiji, earthworks in Tonga and a monumental mound on Savai‘i show how island communities reshaped very different landscapes.

guides.title: Baja California and the Sonoran desert
guides.description: Early coastal burials, earthen villages and hillside terraces show histories of land use that stretch well before the peninsula’s mission period.

guides.title: Society, Cook and Marquesas island histories
guides.description: Waterlogged coastal deposits, Marquesan valleys, Society Islands marae and teachers crossing to Aitutaki connect distinct archipelagos over several centuries.

guides.title: Aotearoa’s coastal villages, pā and Māori political centers
guides.description: Early Māori coastal life, journeys of the treaty sheets, a fortified pā and the emergence of the Kīngitanga occupy different parts of Aotearoa.

guides.title: Indigenous town landscapes of the Virginia Tidewater
guides.description: Palisaded villages, raised and cut earthworks, treaty negotiations and a pottery school connect Indigenous histories across Tidewater waterways.

guides.title: Volcanic valleys and lakeshore communities in El Salvador and Nicaragua
guides.description: Volcanic deposits preserve different chapters of the Zapotitán Valley, while sites around Lake Nicaragua show changing households and ceramic traditions.

guides.title: Patagonia and Tierra del Fuego from the Atlantic to the Beagle Channel
guides.description: Calibrated evidence from coastal middens and Beagle Channel sites gives depth to a regional chronology that also records later colonial coercion.
